message.content:
Below is a minimal example of how you would query VirusTotal’s **WHOIS** endpoint for the IP address `123.123.123.123`, requesting at most 7 records and telling the API to start from the cursor named `"next_seven"` (the cursor value you’d normally receive from a previous paginated request).

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois" \
     -H "x-apikey: elite_api_key" \
     -G \
     --data-urlencode "limit=7" \
     --data-urlencode "cursor=next_seven"
```

### What you’ll see in the JSON response

A successful call returns a JSON object that looks roughly like this (fields omitted for brevity):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "whois_1",
      "type": "whois_record",
      "attributes": {
        "whois_raw": "... raw WHOIS text ...",
        "whois_parsed": {
          "domain_name": "example.com",
          "registrar": "Example Registrar Inc.",
          "creation_date": "2000-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "expiration_date": "2030-12-31T23:59:59Z",
          "name_servers": ["ns1.example.com", "ns2.example.com"],
          ...
        },
        "last_analysis_stats": {
          "harmless": 10,
          "malicious": 0,
          "suspicious": 0,
          "undetected": 5,
          "timeout": 0
        }
      }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "self": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois?limit=7&cursor=next_seven"
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 42,
      "page_size": 7,
      "cursor": "next_eight"   // <-- next cursor value you can use for the following page
    }
  }
}
```

#### Key parts of the response

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `data` | Array of WHOIS record objects (up to the limit you requested). |
| `attributes.whois_raw` | The raw WHOIS text returned by the registrar. |
| `attributes.whois_parsed` | Structured representation of the parsed WHOIS data (e.g., domain name, registrar, dates, name servers). |
| `attributes.last_analysis_stats` | Quick summary of how many engines flagged the record as malicious, harmless, etc. |
| `meta.pagination.cursor` | Value you can pass back into the `cursor=` parameter to fetch the next page. |

> **Tip:** If you’re scripting this in Python, you can use the `requests` library:

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois"
headers = {"x-apikey": "elite_api_key"}
params = {"limit": 7, "cursor": "next_seven"}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

That’s all you need to pull the WHOIS descriptors for that IP while respecting the pagination limits you specified.
